ambiguities.text: Node-configured maximum timeout - no specific maximum value is mandated
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume nodes have implementation-specific maximum timeouts. For security analysis, consider both very short (DoS vector) and very long (resource exhaustion) maximums.

ambiguities.text: Dynamic adjustment based on network conditions is permissible - unclear what network conditions and adjustment mechanisms are valid
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume nodes may adjust timeout defaults based on network congestion, block times, or mempool state. This flexibility could lead to inconsistent behavior across nodes.

ambiguities.text: Missing definition of 'node unready' state - only mentions 'missing nonce, insufficient funds' as examples
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'node unready' includes: missing nonce, insufficient balance, and potentially mempool full or node syncing states.

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes will implement reasonable timeout maximums to prevent resource exhaustion from long-running RPC connections
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious clients could hold open many synchronous connections, exhausting node resources and causing denial of service.

implicit_assumptions.description: The synchronous wait does not block critical node operations or consensus participation
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Heavy usage of this RPC method could cause nodes to fall behind in block processing or miss attestation duties.

implicit_assumptions.description: Network latency and block times are predictable enough for the default 2-second timeout to be meaningful
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: On congested networks, the default timeout may always expire, making the synchronous feature useless.
